title_en: 270: Sports, Markets and Investing: What Separates Skill From Good Luck
title_zh: 270: 体育、市场与投资：技术如何从好运中脱颖而出 | Ronald Van Loon（BlackRock 固定收益）
subtitle_zh: 从网球、足球、篮球到投资，解读微小技术优势如何通过复利产生持久超额收益。
description: 270: Sports, Markets and Investing: What Separates Skill From Good Luck

turns.en: The summer of 2026 has been one that's been dominated by sport. From the World Cup to tennis grand slams and basketball championships, we watched some of the world's best athletes and teams compete at the highest level.
turns.zh: 2026年的夏天，似乎被体育所主导。从世界杯到网球大满贯，再到篮球总冠军赛，我们见证了世界上最优秀的运动员和球队在最高水平上的较量。

turns.en: Behind the headline wins are often remarkably small margins, a handful of decisive points, a slight statistical edge, or a strategy executed more consistently than the competition.
turns.zh: 在那些头条胜利的背后，往往是极其微小的差距——几个关键分，一点统计学上的优势，或者一套比对手执行得更稳定的策略。

turns.en: And there may be a lesson there for investors. Because successful investing isn't necessarily about getting every decision right, it can be about understanding where you have an edge, knowing which decisions matter most, and applying that skill consistently over time.
turns.zh: 而这对投资者来说也许是一堂课。因为成功的投资并不一定要每个决策都做对——而是要理解你的优势在哪里，知道哪些决策最重要，然后持续地运用这些能力。

turns.en: Welcome to The Bit, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 The Bid，我们在这里拆解市场正在发生的事情，探索改变经济和金融格局的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。

turns.en: Today I'm joined by Ronald Van Loon, a portfolio manager in the Global Fixed Income Group at BlackRock. When we last spoke, we explored what tennis could teach us about investing, and why even the greatest players in the world win only slightly more than half the points they play.
turns.zh: 今天和我一起的是 Ronald Van Loon，BlackRock 全球固定收益团队的投资组合经理。我们上次交流时，探讨了网球能教会我们什么投资道理，以及为什么即使是世界上最伟大的球员也只能赢下不到一半的分数。

turns.en: Today we're widening the lens, from World Cup soccer to grand slam tennis and basketball. What can this summer of sport teach us about skill, probability, teamwork, and ultimately successful investing?
turns.zh: 今天我们放大视角，从世界杯足球、大满贯网球到篮球。这个夏天的体育能告诉我们什么关于技术、概率、团队合作，以及最终成功投资的道理？

turns.en: Ronald, thank you so much for joining us on The Bit. Thank you. Thank you very much, Oscar, and thank you for having me back. The last time we spoke was a couple of years ago, and we talked about this interesting intersection between the sport of tennis and investing, and we talked about the surprising idea that some of the greatest tennis players in history win only around 54% of the points that they play.
turns.zh: Ronald，非常感谢你再次来到 The Bid。谢谢。非常感谢你，Oscar，也谢谢你邀请我回来。我们上次交谈还是几年前的事了，当时我们讨论了网球和投资之间有趣的交集，聊了一个让人惊讶的观点——历史上一些最伟大的网球选手只赢了大约54%的分数。

turns.en: In fact, we refer to an infamous commencement speech that Roger Federer made, where he made this exact point. Perfection is impossible. In the 1,526 singles matches I played in my career, I won almost 80% of those matches.
turns.zh: 事实上，我们引用了 Roger Federer 一场很有名的毕业演讲，他在里面精准地表达了这个观点。他说完美是不可能的：在我职业生涯打的1526场单打比赛中，我赢了将近80%的比赛。

turns.en: What percentage of points do you think I won in those matches? Only 54%. Now you've continued your research since then, and before we widen this out to other sports, remind us why that relatively small edge can produce such dominant results over time.
turns.zh: 你觉得我在那些比赛中赢了百分之多少的分？只有54%。你后来继续做了研究，在我们把这个话题拓展到其他运动之前，帮我们回忆一下为什么这么小的优势能随着时间产生如此主导的结果。

turns.en: I think tennis is a great analogy to the world of investing. So if you take Federer as an example, over the full length of his tennis career, he won more than 80% of the matches that he ever played.
turns.zh: 我觉得网球是投资非常好的类比。就拿 Federer 来说，在他整个网球生涯中，他赢了超过80%的比赛。

turns.en: But then, as he famously said, if you look at it per point, he only won around 54% of the points he ever played, which is really low, only marginally above a coin toss.
turns.zh: 但正如他著名地说过的那样，如果你逐分来看，他只赢了大约54%的分，这个数字真的很低，仅仅比抛硬币高那么一点。

turns.en: And that's really surprising. Now, that's nothing to do with Roger Federer. That's really in the game of tennis. If you look at all the greats, whether it's men's or women's tennis, you get those same statistics coming back time and time again.
turns.zh: 这真的很令人惊讶。这并不是 Roger Federer 个人的问题——这是网球这项运动本身的特点。如果你去看所有伟大球员，不管是男子还是女子网球，你会一次又一次看到相同的数据。

turns.en: So even today, if I think about Sinner and Alkarast, the big player in men's tennis, they have very similar numbers, about per point success rate of just north of 54%.
turns.zh: 所以即使到今天，如果我想到 Sinner 和 Alcaraz，男子网坛的顶尖球员，他们的数据也非常类似，每分胜率大约在54%以上。

turns.en: But of course, the pair of them have won 10 out of the 12 Grand Slam tournaments of the last three years. How about that? How about that? And the reason for that really is in tennis, you have lots of opportunities to score.
turns.zh: 但他们两个人赢得了过去三年12个大满贯赛事中的10个。怎么样？怎么样？而这背后的原因确实在于，网球中你有大量的得分机会。

turns.en: You have a tournament, several matches, matches made up of sets, a set is made up of games, a game is made up of points. Each of these is an opportunity to express a difference in skill.
turns.zh: 你有锦标赛、多场比赛、比赛由盘组成、一盘由局组成、一局由分组成。每一个环节都是一个展示技术差异的机会。

turns.en: And then once you start adding these kind of measurement points together, it starts compounding up and you end up with a very high probability of winning the match, like in Federer's case, 80%.
turns.zh: 然后当你开始把这些度量点累加起来，就会复利叠加，最终得到非常高的获胜概率——像 Federer 那样，80%。

turns.en: Now in investing, we have a similar dynamic. I'm a portfolio manager. We make many investment decisions continuously, buy, sell, hold, the timing, sizing decisions.
turns.zh: 在投资中，我们也有类似的动态。我是投资组合经理。我们不断地做很多投资决策：买入、卖出、持有、时机、仓位。

turns.en: They make these decisions all the time. And of course, after the fact, you can look back and see, has this been a successful decision or not and start doing the same analysis like we just did on the tennis match.
turns.zh: 我们一直在做这些决策。当然，事后你可以回头看——这个决策成功了还是没成功——然后开始做类似我们刚才对网球比赛做的分析。

turns.en: And you come up with some remarkable similarities. For example, we worked out what percentage of the total investment decisions do you need to get right in order to get outperformance.
turns.zh: 你会发现一些惊人的相似之处。比如，我们算出来你需要做对多大比例的投资决策才能跑赢大盘。

turns.en: The actual percentage there is 53%. That's remarkably similar to tennis. You have that same effect of a fairly low amount of skill per decision.
turns.zh: 实际的比例是53%。这跟网球惊人地相似。同样的效应——每次决策中的技术优势相当小。

turns.en: But as you compound them over many different decisions, it starts compounding up into durable success. There's this remarkable commonality between tennis and the world of investing that you've helped uncover.
turns.zh: 但当你在众多不同的决策中把它们复利叠加起来，就会增长为持久的成功。网球和投资世界之间有你帮我们揭示的这种惊人的共通性。

turns.en: And while we had focused on Roger Federer in the last discussion, you're saying that there are other premier tennis players who have this phenomenon of winning just over half of their points, but yet being very dominant in terms of the end results.
turns.zh: 而我们上次主要关注的是 Roger Federer，你现在说的是还有其他顶级网球选手也有这种现象——赢了刚好超过一半的分，但在最终结果上非常有统治力。

turns.en: As I mentioned, you've continued some of your research since the last time we spoke and your latest research goes a step further and looks at not just how often investors get decisions, right, but what happens when they do.
turns.zh: 我之前提到过，你自上次交流以来继续做了一些研究，而你最新的研究更进一步，不仅关注投资者做对决策的频率，还关注他们做对时会发生什么。

turns.en: And you talk about this concept of winning the big points, maybe elaborate a little bit more on what you mean by that. Yeah, of course, in sports, like all sports, you have these crucial episodes, the real pivotal moments, like in tennis, the break points, the set points, and so forth, when perhaps you see somewhat of a difference.
turns.zh: 你谈到了'赢下关键分'这个概念，也许可以多展开说说你指的是什么。当然了，在运动中——所有运动中——都有那些关键的时刻、真正决定性的节点。比如网球中的破发点、盘点等等——也许在这些时刻你会看到一些差别。

turns.en: And in tennis, you can really see winning the big points brings you that extra level of success. And in investing, there are certainly similarities.
turns.zh: 在网球中你确实能看到，赢下关键分能带给你额外的成功水平。在投资中，确实也有类似之处。

turns.en: In tennis, for example, if you look at it, Federer are all the big players and just isolate on those kind of pivotal moments, the break points, the set points, and all of a sudden you see those conversion percentages creep up to low 60%, but it's still not super high, but there's definitely a difference.
turns.zh: 在网球中，比如你去看 Federer 和其他大牌球员，单独隔离那些关键时刻——破发点、盘点——突然间你会看到转化率上升到接近60%，虽然也不是特别高，但确实有差别。

turns.en: So you see the real difference between the absolute top players and the other really good players in terms of winning those big points. And in investing, we did the same kind of analysis, we looked at what drives really the outcome of the investment process in terms of success.
turns.zh: 所以你就能看到绝对顶尖球员和其他非常好的球员之间的真正区别——在于赢下那些关键分的能力。在投资中，我们做了类似的分析，去看究竟是什么驱动投资过程在成功层面的结果。

turns.en: Is it about having more success in each individual decision, making more successful investment decisions, or is it around converting whenever you're successful into a better payout profile?
turns.zh: 是每次个人决策的成功率更高——做出更多成功的投资决策——还是当你做对的时候把它转化为更好的回报结构？

turns.en: And then, of course, in investing, it's the same as in tennis. Those two things need to be looked at in conjunction. So you really need to think about these two things together.
turns.zh: 然后当然，在投资中和网球一样。这两者需要被放在一起考虑。你真的需要把这两件事结合起来思考。

turns.en: So there's no point in investing in focusing only on your hit rate or only on your payoff ratio. You really need to look at them together. And the other thing is, both play a role and both can be actually fairly small in size, in isolation.
turns.zh: 所以在投资中，只关注你的命中率或者只关注你的盈亏比没有意义。你真的需要把它们放在一起看。另一个点是，两者都起作用，而且单独来看都可以相当小。

turns.en: The real key point is to let them compound over time, so make more investment decisions. And like in tennis, let those small skill levels compound over time to lead into durable outcomes.
turns.zh: 真正的关键点是让它们随时间复利增长——做更多的投资决策。就像在网球中一样，让那些微小的技术水平随着时间复利，带来持久的结果。

turns.en: And I think one of the points you're also making here is that the really elite tennis players, there are, as you say, the big points. There are certain parts of the match where winning that point has a bigger impact on performance.
turns.zh: 我觉得你这里表达的另一个观点是，真正的精英网球选手——就像你说的，关键分——比赛中的某些部分，赢下那一分对表现有更大的影响。

turns.en: And I think you're saying that the elite investors, there are certain investment decisions that are really crucial to get right. And the really elite investors do get those right and therefore leads them to better outcomes in their portfolios over time.
turns.zh: 我想你是在说，精英投资者也有一些投资决策是真正关键、必须做对的。真正精英的投资者确实能把这些关键决策做对，因此带来了长期更好的组合表现。

turns.en: I think really you need to look at those three things in conjunction. So getting more decisions right and you get wrong, once you get a decision right, make sure you convert that into kind of a meaningful performance number.
turns.zh: 我觉得你真的需要把三件事放在一起看。第一，做对更多决策、犯更少错误；第二，一旦你做对了一个决策，确保你把它转化为有意义的业绩数字。

turns.en: And then the third element is play that game often enough to have that same compounding effect like you have in tennis. So Ronald, we talk a lot about tennis, which is a unique sport in that it gives the athletes hundreds of opportunities to express their skill.
turns.zh: 然后第三个要素是要足够频繁地参与游戏，让它有和网球一样的复利效应。Ronald，我们聊了很多网球——网球是一项很独特的运动，它给了运动员无数次展示技术的得分机会。

turns.en: But that's not true of every sport. If we think about the sport of soccer or football, which took center stage this past summer in the US and Canada and Mexico, that's a different sport.
turns.zh: 但并不是每项运动都如此。如果我们想想足球——今夏在美国、加拿大和墨西哥登上舞台中央的那项运动——那是不同的运动。

turns.en: That is one where it can be decided by just one or two moments. So when you think about that contrast of tennis versus a sport like soccer or football, what does that tell us about the relationship between skill and chance?
turns.zh: 它可能只由一到两个瞬间就能决定胜负。所以当你思考网球与足球的对比时，这对技术与运气之间的关系告诉我们什么？

turns.en: And does the same principle apply to investing? You're right. It's a completely different sport, actually almost at the opposite side of the spectrum.
turns.zh: 同样的原则是否也适用于投资？你说得对，这确实是一项完全不同的运动，几乎在另一个极端。

turns.en: It has very few opportunities to score a nil-nil score line or one nil and so forth. That's not uncommon. So you typically have those kind of low score lines or low opportunities to score.
turns.zh: 它很少有得分机会——0比0、1比0这样的比分并不罕见。所以你通常看到的都是这种低比分或者很少的得分机会。

turns.en: And what that means is that indeed on match level, that means that the influence of chance is indeed higher in football than it is in tennis.
turns.zh: 这意味着什么呢——在单场比赛层面，运气的影响确实在足球中比在网球中更大。

turns.en: So in football, it's by no means given that the better team, so to say, wins the game. And perhaps that kind of unpredictability adds a little to the kind of the earlier or the kind of the popularity of the sport.
turns.zh: 所以在足球中，更好的球队赢得比赛并不是必然的。也许这种不可预测性也增加了这项运动的刺激感和受欢迎程度。

turns.en: But if you zoom out a little and go on World Cup level, so obviously you play multiple matches, then you see that same effect starting to appear again.
turns.zh: 但如果你稍微拉远一点，到世界杯层面——显然你要打多场比赛——你就会看到同样的效应开始重新出现。

turns.en: So for example, if you think about the World Cup that was played this summer, the four semifinalists, right, is Spain, Argentina, England and France, they were the four favorites going into the tournament.
turns.zh: 比如，想想今夏的世界杯，四个半决赛队伍——西班牙、阿根廷、英格兰和法国——他们就是赛前被看好的四支热门。

turns.en: So you're right, on individual match level, there is much less of a low skill effect that you can see there. But once you start adding those up into tournament level or into national competition level, you see that same effect appearing over and over again, like in tennis, like in investing.
turns.zh: 所以你说得对，在单场比赛层面，技术优势没那么明显。但一旦你把它们累加到锦标赛或国家队比赛层面，同样的效应就会一次又一次出现——就像网球，就像投资。

turns.en: Right. There's a different lens that you have to apply when trying to compare one sport to the next and apply those findings to what you're seeing in the investment world.
turns.zh: 对。在比较不同运动并将发现应用到投资世界时，你需要换一个不同的视角。

turns.en: Let's keep talking about sports. And one of the things that is another contrast between soccer and tennis, I'm going to say soccer because I'm based here in the U.S. Ronald, I know you're based in the U.K., so you're probably wanting to correct me.
turns.zh: 让我们继续聊运动。足球和网球之间还有一个对比——我要说足球了，因为我住在美国。Ronald，我知道你住在英国，所以你大概想纠正我。

turns.en: But when we compare those two sports, there's another difference, which is this concept of the team. This is a more individual sport, soccer is obviously more of a team sport, and investing can sometimes be portrayed as being about one great decision maker making the call.
turns.zh: 但当我们比较这两项运动时，还有一个不同——就是'团队'的概念。网球更偏向个人运动，足球显然是团队运动，而投资有时候被描绘成靠一个伟大的决策者来做判断。

turns.en: But in reality, how important is the team around them to producing the consistent investment outcomes? I think perhaps the best illustration of the team approach in football is perhaps the winner, Spain won the World Cup, they've played eight matches, they scored 14 goals, they conceded one.
turns.zh: 但在现实中，身边的团队对于产生持续的投资成果有多重要？我觉得足球中团队方式最好的例子也许是冠军——西班牙赢了世界杯，打了八场比赛，进了14个球，只丢了一个。

turns.en: So that already gives you a ratio that perhaps you think, oh, that's obviously goals for goals against, perhaps that's a very defensive game.
turns.zh: 这已经给了你一个比率，你可能会想，进球对失球——那可能是一个很保守的打法。

turns.en: But actually the way that the team plays is not defensive at all. I was kind of highlight three elements to it. One of them is the possession of the football.
turns.zh: 但实际上这支球队的踢法一点都不保守。我想强调三个要素。一个是控球率。

turns.en: So they play at around a 64% possession that's much higher than the other teams typically in football. They also have that possession a little bit higher up the pitch than it's normal.
turns.zh: 他们的控球率大约在64%，远高于足球中其他球队通常的水平。而且他们的控球位置也比通常更靠前。

turns.en: And in the words of my footballing hero, Johan Cruyff, he said famously, if your opponent doesn't have the ball, then they can't score against you either.
turns.zh: 用我心目中足球英雄 Johan Cruyff 的话说，他有一句名言：如果对手没有球，他们就没法对你进球。

turns.en: And then the third element, of course, is the pass rate, and the way that Spain played had a comfortably much higher than average pass rate and also much higher than average successful pass rate.
turns.zh: 然后第三个要素，当然是传球率——西班牙的踢法有远高于平均水平的传球率，也有远高于平均水平的传球成功率。

turns.en: So that's a very unique style of playing and very different to the other four semifinals. And obviously it proves successful. I think you can translate that over to the world of investing as well.
turns.zh: 那是一种非常独特的踢法，和其他四支半决赛球队非常不同。而且显然证明是成功的。我觉得这可以转化到投资世界。

turns.en: I'm a bond manager. I work in Fixed Income. In the words of our CIO, Rick Reeder, he says there's something like one and a half million Fixed Income securities in the world.
turns.zh: 我是债券经理，我在固定收益领域工作。用我们 CIO Rick Rieder 的话说，全世界大概有150万种固定收益证券。

turns.en: That's an enormous breadth and width of investment options you have on the table there. It's pretty obvious you are not very likely to win that game with a star striker approach or with a long ball.
turns.zh: 那是巨大的投资选择广度。很明显，靠一个明星前锋的打法或者长传冲吊是不可能赢下那场比赛的。

turns.en: You're really going to have to win that game through the team because simply the width and the breadth of the investment opportunities are too broad.
turns.zh: 你真的必须通过团队来赢下那场比赛，因为投资机会的宽度和广度实在太大了。

turns.en: So indeed we have specialists each of their own function. We have credit analysts looking at the credits. We have risk managers looking at position sizing.
turns.zh: 所以我们确实有各自领域的专家。我们有信用分析师看信用，有风控经理看仓位。

turns.en: We have traders looking at execution. And then we can pass the security, so to say, in between these specialists. So I think there's clearly an analogy there.
turns.zh: 我们有交易员看执行。然后我们可以在这些专家之间传递证券。所以我觉得这里面确实有类比。

turns.en: My own way to think about it is that there's one and a half million Fixed Income securities in the world that offers you one and a half million opportunities to score.
turns.zh: 我自己的理解方式是：全世界有150万种固定收益证券，那就给了你150万次得分机会。

turns.en: Right. And going back to the beginning of our conversation, you don't necessarily have to make every single decision the right decision. In other words, in a portfolio, you may not own one and a half million securities.
turns.zh: 对。回到我们对话的开始，你不必让每一个决策都做对。换句话说，一个组合里你不可能持有150万种证券。

turns.en: That's unlikely. You're going to own far less than that. But there still gives you a lot of chances where you could get either the right decision or the wrong decision.
turns.zh: 那不太可能。你持有的会远少于此。但即便如此，你还是有很多机会——可以做对或者做错。

turns.en: But so long as you're getting a little bit more than half of the decisions right, you're probably trending in the right direction. So let's keep talking about sports.
turns.zh: 但只要你能做对略多于一半的决策，你就大概率在正确的方向上。好，我们继续聊运动。

turns.en: The Olympics are coming up in 2028. And the Olympics are interesting because for many athletes, there's years of preparation that come down to a single race, a single match or a single performance.
turns.zh: 奥运会将在2028年到来。奥运会很有意思，因为对很多运动员来说，多年的准备都浓缩在一场比赛、一次对决或一次表现中。

turns.en: And that's, again, very different from tennis where you have hundreds of opportunities to score. So what can that teach us about preparation and decision making when you may only have one opportunity to get it right?
turns.zh: 这又一次和网球非常不同——网球有无数次得分机会。那么当你可能只有一次机会做到最好的时候，这对准备和决策有什么启示？

turns.en: Yes. Of course, it's super different to the world of investing, right? In investing, you are measured continuously almost. In the Olympics, as you say, you have that one moment, one moment in time that you prepare for a long time.
turns.zh: 是的，当然，这和投资的非常不一样，对吧？在投资中，你几乎是持续被衡量的。在奥运会中，如你所说，你只有一个时刻，一个你准备了很久的时刻。

turns.en: But I think it's quite interesting how the world of sports itself has adjusted to deal with that challenge. If you look at some of the Olympic sports, particularly perhaps the ones that are a bit less popular, that don't have like annual international tournaments, the way how those sports are set up is that particularly in the year prior to the Olympics, you see a sudden increase in the amount of international tournaments.
turns.zh: 但我觉得很有趣的是，体育界本身是如何调整来应对这个挑战的。如果你看一些奥运项目——特别是一些没那么流行的、没有年度国际赛事的项目——你会发现这些运动的赛制安排是这样的：特别是在奥运前一年，国际赛事的数量会突然增加。

turns.en: Think about qualification tournaments, ranking tournaments. So what these tournaments offer to the participant is really two things. One, the opportunity to learn about yourself and where your skill is.
turns.zh: 想想资格赛、排名赛。这些赛事为参赛者提供的是两样东西。第一，了解自己的机会——你的技术水平到底在哪里。

turns.en: And two, the opportunity to learn about the skill of your opponent. And that really makes the Olympics itself like an outcome of a process, the actual match or whatever they participate in is the outcome.
turns.zh: 第二，了解对手技术水平的机会。这真的让奥运会本身更像是一个过程的结果——实际的比赛或他们参与的项目是结果。

turns.en: And is then that pre-Olympic circuit really that is the process through which you learn about your relative skill. And there's a similarity then or a parallel to an investment process that an investment team would use.
turns.zh: 而那些奥运前的巡回赛才是真正的过程——通过这些过程你了解了自己的相对技术。这和团队投资流程有一个相似之处。

turns.en: And you mentioned you're a bond manager, a fixed income manager. There is a process behind the scenes that you're following to try and increase your chances of success.
turns.zh: 你说过你是债券经理、固定收益经理。在幕后有一个你遵循的流程来尝试增加你成功的机会。

turns.en: Yes, absolutely. Continuous learning and continuous adapting to the environment because not only your own relative skill changes, it's also your opponents changes all the time.
turns.zh: 是的，绝对的。持续学习、持续适应环境——因为不仅是你的相对技术在变化，对手也一直在变化。

turns.en: So that continuously learning process means that you have to all the time adjust. So again, we've continued to broaden the conversation. When we originally spoke, Ronald, it was about tennis and we started there.
turns.zh: 所以那个持续学习的过程意味着你必须不断调整。好，我们再次拓宽了对话的范围。我们最初交谈时，Ronald，是从网球开始的。

turns.en: We've talked about soccer. We've talked about the World Cup and team-based approaches. We've talked about the Olympics, which introduces this concept of a process that you need to follow to therefore be ready for that singular match or game or event that you've been building towards.
turns.zh: 我们聊了足球，聊了世界杯和团队合作，聊了奥运会——它引入了一个概念：你需要遵循一个过程，才能为那个你一直在为之准备的单一比赛或赛事做好准备。

turns.en: But let's talk about basketball, which has given us plenty to talk about. Those of us based here in New York, like myself, the New York Knicks won the NBA championship this summer.
turns.zh: 但让我们聊聊篮球，它也给了我们很多话题。我们住在这里纽约的人——像我一样——纽约尼克斯队今年夏天赢了 NBA 总冠军。

turns.en: And I can certainly tell you, Ronald, that New York was a buzz when that took place. Basketball is unique in that it gives us another way of thinking about decision-making because not every shot offers the same potential reward.
turns.zh: 我完全可以告诉你，Ronald，那发生时整个纽约都沸腾了。篮球很独特，因为它给了我们另一种思考决策的方式——不是每一投都提供相同的潜在回报。

turns.en: There are ways in which to score two points in basketball or in some cases three points. So how should investors think about the trade-off between the probability of being right and the potential payoff when they are?
turns.zh: 篮球中有得两分的方式，某些情况下也有得三分的方式。那么投资者应该如何思考'做对的概率'和'做对时的潜在回报'之间的权衡？

turns.en: Yeah, that's a super interesting basketball and it is also a great analogy. So if you think about the game of basketball today and then compare it to maybe how the NBA was 20 years ago, there has definitely been a big change.
turns.zh: 是的，篮球超级有趣，也是一个很好的类比。如果你想想今天的篮球比赛，然后和20年前 NBA 的样子比一比——确实发生了巨大的变化。

turns.en: For example, two decades ago, the number of three-point attempts that were made just beyond the circle in basketball was about 17% of total shots.
turns.zh: 比如，二十年前，三分线外出手的次数大约占总投篮的17%。

turns.en: And if you translate that to the NBA game today, that's more than double, that is 40%. So that means is that the percentage of shot attempts that are being made just beyond the three-point line is more than doubled.
turns.zh: 如果你把这个数字转化到今天的 NBA，那已经是翻了一倍多了——达到了40%。也就是说，三分线外出手的比例翻了一倍还多。

turns.en: The number of shot attempts that are made just below the basket is just about the same and it's really that mid-range, really, where you see a decrease.
turns.zh: 在篮下出手的次数基本没变。真正减少的是中距离——你在那里看到了明显的下降。

turns.en: So the two-point jumper, so to say. That's exactly the reason why that is a trade-off between the probability of making the shot and the payoff of when you do make the shot.
turns.zh: 就是那个两分跳投。这恰恰说明了这是一个投篮命中概率和命中时回报之间的权衡。

turns.en: Obviously, it is a bit more difficult to take a three-point shot and be successful in that than it is a two-point shot, but as you rightly say, your payoff is 50% higher.
turns.zh: 显然，投三分比投两分更难成功，但正如你所说，你的回报高了50%。

turns.en: So once you actually start translating that into expected value, so to say, probability times payoff, then indeed the game has shown that it's the three-point shots and the right underneath the basket shots.
turns.zh: 所以当你真正把期望值算出来——概率乘以回报——那么确实，数据证明了三分出手和篮下投篮的期望值最高。

turns.en: The expected value is the highest and the game has migrated very much the same as the analogy as we just had in tennis or we just had in football.
turns.zh: 比赛已经朝这个方向迁移了，和我们刚才在网球和足球中的类比如出一辙。

turns.en: You need to look at the probability of scoring and look at the payoff, marry those together, and then last point, of course, is look at how many shots attempts you can possibly make and you can really see the game of basketball has really migrated on those three same dimensions to a different game today than it was two decades ago.
turns.zh: 你需要看得分概率、看回报、把两者结合，然后最后一点——看你最多能有多少次出手——你真的能看到篮球比赛在这三个相同的维度上完全迁移了，和二十年前已经是完全不同的比赛了。

turns.en: Ronald, when you put all of this together, again, from the small edges that you get from a sport like tennis, which provides hundreds of opportunities in a match to the teamwork element of soccer, the different potential payoffs from a sport like basketball, what is it that elite sport ultimately teaches us about becoming a better investor?
turns.zh: Ronald，当你把所有这些放在一起看——从网球这样一场比赛有无数次机会的小优势，到足球中的团队合作，再到篮球不同的潜在回报——精英运动最终教会我们什么关于成为更好投资者的道理？

turns.en: If you look at the three sports, really look at them together, I think there's some big lessons to take away as an investor. You can almost break it up in three bits.
turns.zh: 如果你看这三项运动，真正把它们放在一起看——我觉得作为投资者有一些大的教训可以汲取。你可以把它分成三个部分。

turns.en: You look at the probability of success per investment decision. You look at the payoff profile of the investment decisions was the payoff if you're successful was the payoff if you are unsuccessful.
turns.zh: 第一，你看每次投资决策的成功概率。第二，你看投资决策的回报结构——成功时的回报和失败时的回报。

turns.en: And then lastly is the number of goal attempts, not the number of the investment decisions that the game provides you. And I think the key message really here is bit like in basketball, you need to look at these together.
turns.zh: 然后最后是出手次数——或者说这项运动给你的投资机会数量。我觉得这里的关键信息确实就像篮球一样——你需要把这些放在一起看。

turns.en: There's no point in focusing on just one aspect of that equation, you need to look at all three together and choose your optimum that works for you across all these three dimensions together.
turns.zh: 只关注那个等式的一个方面没有意义，你需要把三者一起看，在这三个维度上找到适合你的最优点。

turns.en: And I think the second point, which is really valid, is that the investment skill you need to have per investment decision needs to be only marginally above a coin toss.
turns.zh: 然后第二点，我认为非常有道理——就是你在每个投资决策上需要的技术水平只需要比抛硬币略高一点点。

turns.en: As long as of course you let them compound over time, it's a bit like in tennis, as you let these investment decisions compound over time, you only need to be successful 53-54 percent of the time.
turns.zh: 当然前提是你让它们随时间复利增长。就像网球一样，当你让投资决策随时间复利，你只需要有53%到54%的成功率就够了。

turns.en: And that leads you to these kind of durable high wind rates over the long term. Well, all the sports that we've talked about are definitely contact sports.
turns.zh: 这就能带给你长期持续的高胜率。好了，我们聊到的所有这些运动都是身体对抗性很强的运动。

turns.en: Ronald, you and I have worked in the markets for many years, and I think we can attest to the fact that investing is also a full contact sport.
turns.zh: Ronald，你我都在市场里工作了很多年，我想我们可以证实投资也是一项全对抗运动。

turns.en: Volatility that will introduce itself once in a while, that can make it a very emotional exercise, but having discipline and thinking about some of the process and relying on your team, some of the things that you've talked about will help.
turns.zh: 波动性时不时会出现，可以让它变成一件非常情绪化的事，但有纪律性、思考流程、依靠团队——你聊到的一些东西会有帮助。

turns.en: Ronald, I'm just curious, when you go and attend a sporting match, can you just enjoy the game or is your mind racing about the analogy to investing?
turns.zh: Ronald，我很好奇，当你去看一场体育比赛时，你能单纯地享受比赛吗，还是脑子里一直在转投资的类比？

turns.en: Yes, you have to ask the people that join me, and I've heard that comment once or twice, so I think you're probably onto something there. I'm sure your mind is spinning, but we're thankful that it is because you've given us a lot of great analogies and a lot of great comparisons between sport and investing.
turns.zh: 是的，你得问那些跟我一起去看比赛的人，我听到过一两次这样的评论了，所以我觉得你可能说到点子上了。我相信你的脑子一定在飞速运转，但我们很感谢如此，因为你给了我们太多精彩的类比——运动和投资之间的。

turns.en: Thank you for rejoining us on the bid to talk about this topic, and we look forward to having you back when you have another great story to tell us about these two themes together.
turns.zh: 感谢你再次来到 The Bid 聊这个话题，我们期待当你又有一个关于这两个主题的好故事时再邀请你回来。

turns.en: Ronald, thank you again for joining us. Thank you very much. Thanks for listening to this episode of The Bid. Next up, I'm speaking with David Rubenstein, co-founder of the Carlisle Group and owner of the Baltimore Orioles, about his new book, Inside the Owner's Box, where we'll discuss the civic role of teams, lessons he's learned in leadership, and the opportunities and risks shaping the future of sports ownership.
turns.zh: Ronald，再次感谢你来。非常感谢。感谢收听本期 The Bid。下一期，我将和 David Rubenstein 对谈——他是 Carlyle Group 的联合创始人、Baltimore Orioles 的老板——聊他的新书 Inside the Owner's Box，我们会讨论球队的城市角色、他在领导力上学到的教训，以及塑造体育所有权未来的机遇和风险。
